title: Vector merge: incremental fold (avoid full layer re-arrangement per stroke on dense art)
description: Follow-up from P5 cutover (task 1323). planarMergeCommit/foldShapeIntoLayer rebuilds the ENTIRE layer arrangement (buildArrangementFromShapes over every mergeable shape) on each commit. Measured one-stroke fold cost on a dense solid-fill shape: n=100 -> 35ms, n=400 -> 61ms, n=800 -> 176ms (super-linear). A traced-bitmap layer (1000+ solid fills, all mergeable) thus sees a ~250-400ms hitch per stroke. NOT a correctness blocker (all 8 oracles diff=0; normal art is responsive), but on dense art the merge 'rebuilds the world' per stroke. Options: (a) only fold the new shape against shapes whose bbox overlaps it (skip disjoint fills); (b) incremental insertEdge into a cached live arrangement instead of rebuild-from-scratch; (c) keep traced-bitmap shapes as non-merging until explicitly broken-apart. Acceptance: per-stroke fold on a 1000-fill layer under ~50ms, oracles still diff=0.
